title: Father of All! Where Shall We Find
description: Father of All! Where Shall We Find in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Edmund Butcher wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 50 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christian Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther of all! where shall we find A tem-ple suit-ed to thy praise? To thee, the un-cre-at-ed Mind, What earth-ly al-tar shall we raise?

lines: Father of all! where shall we find
A temple suited to thy praise?
What earthly altar shall we raise?
And gladly seek the house of prayer;
There thy salvation we have found,
And still, O God, we'll seek it there.
From breast to breast the holy flame
Shall kindle round the sacred place:
At once we'll hymn our Father's name,
At once we'll seek our Father's face.
To meet us with peculiar love;
And when the hymns of earth shall end,
We'll give thee nobler hymns above.

licence: Public domain: Edmund Butcher died in 1822.
credits: Words by Edmund Butcher (1757–1822), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
